title: Where is the patient? ED-to-ward location visibility for Inpatient Pharmacy
source: Poster: 'The Problem / Why It Matters / Proposed Solution / How to Update PHIS Location / Our Objective'

lines.text: When a patient is admitted for ward care, they may still remain in the Emergency Department —
for example, while waiting for a bed.
Inpatient Pharmacy needs to know where that patient actually is.
Today, the way to find out is to call ED.
Is the patient still here, or already in the ward?
The patient's location affects Pharmacy's workflow: order processing, verification and dispensing.
Checking manually adds delay, workload, and the risk of outdated information.
For patients planned for ward admission who need to stay in ED, register them in PHIS under Kecemasan & Trauma (Admission).
Visit type: Inpatient. Department: Gen Med.
lines.speak: Visit type, Inpatient. Department, Gen Med.

lines.text: While the patient is still in ED, the PHIS location shows Kecemasan & Trauma (Admission).
When the patient enters the receiving ward, the location is updated to the actual ward.
Under the proposal, the update is made in Visit Management, in eight steps.
Find the patient, edit the visit, select the new ward location in the Transfer Detail List, and save.
Today, Pharmacy calls ED to ask where the patient is.
Under the proposal, the PHIS location itself shows whether the patient is still in ED, or in the ward.
The objective: give Inpatient Pharmacy a reliable way to tell whether an admitted patient is still in ED,
or has moved to the receiving ward — with the minimum additional workload.
